date_str_investigation.note_on_poisoning_confound: C1 through K ran on ONE native context that was never reloaded (Fast Refresh preserved DateStrProbeScreen's contextRef across all those edits) - after C1's genuine first failure, every later result on that context is potentially confounded by context poisoning (one failed grammar compile corrupting the native sampler state for all subsequent calls). This was discovered mid-investigation (see poisonCheck) and every finding from L onward was re-verified on a freshly force-stopped/relaunched app (a brand-new native context, first call only) specifically to rule this out. C1's original failure and every L-P result are poisoning-safe; D1-K's results, while individually re-confirmed fresh where it mattered (G, H), should be read as directionally consistent with the fresh re-tests rather than independently authoritative.

Model even generated a real, correctly-formatted date. This is what was applied to task_extraction.v1.gbnf and coaching_resolution.v1.gbnf.

verdict.root_cause: For a jchar{m,n}-based rule (the alternation+repetition primitive backing every bounded string field), the rule name referenced from its parent must exactly match its own JSON key text, or llama.cpp's GBNF parser on this build rejects the whole grammar at parse time. Mechanism not further isolated within this session's scope - empirically characterized and reproducibly confirmed (N=2 fresh runs each for the two decisive contrasts: title/{1,80} passes, foo_str/{1,80} with mismatched naming fails), but why a context-free grammar parser would exhibit this is unexplained. Ruled out as explanations: bound value (10 through 80 all fail with mismatched naming; 80 passes with matched naming), exact-count vs range repetition, indirection depth, character classes vs literal alternation, the specific string 'date'/'date_str', context poisoning, and llama.rn's jinja auto-grammar override.
verdict.fix_applied: Renamed date_str to date in both task_extraction.v1.gbnf (due_on_date) and coaching_resolution.v1.gbnf (until_on_date), matching each rule's own "date" JSON key, and gave it its own quote literals (title/description shape) instead of relying on the parent rule's literal to supply them. Bound loosened from a structural [0-9]{4}"-"[0-9]{2}"-"[0-9]{2} to jchar{1,10} - digit/dash format enforcement moves entirely to the zod validator, which already independently regex-checks ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$ in both validator.ts files (confirmed before applying the fix - this was not a new gap opened by relaxing the grammar).
verdict.not_fixed_flagged_for_followup: coaching_resolution.v1.gbnf has three more jchar-based fields whose rule name does not match their own JSON key: changes_notes (key "approach_notes"), reason120 (key "reason", used twice), condition120 (key "condition"). These were discovered via this session's root-cause finding but NOT tested or fixed - same bug pattern, same fix (rename to match key), needs its own confirmation pass before applying.
